packs.title: Collections, public rooms and park views
packs.promise: Compare actual museum evidence, make original pages and explore bounded public park settings.

q.s: Keep visible display choices beside the environments they describe.
st: Enter the opened natural-history galleries with required admission. Locate the limestone-cave, Texas-forest and Cretaceous-Sea settings that are actually available today.

At each setting, record one visible spatial or material choice and paraphrase one environmental relationship explained by the display. Treat a reconstruction as a display, not a living habitat or direct view of the past.
Compare two records: what does the presentation make easy to notice, and what depends on interpretation? Do not use the mammoth replica as a substitute for one of these three settings.
Write three setting records and your comparison after exit if needed. Use your own words rather than copying a panel, mural or exhibit illustration.

q.s: Make an original page from a remembered spatial contrast.
st: Visit an actually opened public museum gallery. Notice one spatial contrast in the presentation, such as the distance between objects or how an available wall meets an open viewing area.
Remember the contrast in plain words. Do not copy an artwork, artist statement, title, photograph, composition or a real person’s voice.

After leaving, write an original four-line response built from two everyday shapes or spaces of your own choosing. Use the remembered contrast as a starting rule, rather than describing or imitating an artist’s work.
Add one sentence explaining the contrast you used and how your original page follows it. Keep a private response; no posting, performance, purchase or staff conversation is needed.

q.s: Notice a changed view on the same bounded park path.
st: Start at the open public concrete junction south of the pavilion-side path. Check the available visitor path and turn point before setting off; do not enter a reserved pavilion or service area.
Follow the bounded concrete path to its pavilion junction, about 164 metres one way in the retained map. Notice one path-edge or view relationship without approaching the river edge.
Turn at that public junction and return on the same path. Notice how the same relationship looks in the opposite direction; a small or absent change is a valid result.
Write one outward observation, one return observation and a sentence comparing them. Finish at your starting junction; onward transport is arranged separately.

packs.title: Downtown street fronts and a suspended crossing
packs.promise: Connect an admitted museum, civic street fronts and an open Saturday market with a one-way bridge crossing and house tour.

q.t: Three links in a civic square
q.s: Collect how three available public-space features connect.
st: Enter an open public path in the square and choose three available feature relationships, such as a bench beside a path, a planting edge beside a paved area or a route leading toward an open entrance.
For each, record one visible connection and what movement or pause it could support. Describe the form rather than claiming how every visitor uses it.
Compare two records: which connection is clearest from your position, and which needs a change of viewpoint along the lawful path? Do not copy a public sculpture or inscription.
Write three public-space links and one comparison from an available place clear of circulation. A dry or inactive water feature is not a failed visit if the required available links can be observed.

q.t: Three records from an open market
q.s: Collect how actual displays arrange available goods.
st: Reach the actual operating Bridge Street Plaza market before its published closing time. Choose three presently offered displays you can view without blocking trade.

For each, record one visible arrangement relationship, such as a container beside a grouped item or a repeated display shape. Describe what is available without guessing origin, ingredients, farming methods or a seller’s story.
Compare two records in one sentence. If a display is screened, proprietary or requires handling, choose another available display rather than seeking extra access.
Write three display-arrangement records and your comparison after stepping clear of stalls. Finish before closure; no purchase, product photo, copied label or conversation is needed.

q.s: Compare the approach and midpoint of one pedestrian deck crossing.
st: At the open east deck end, confirm that the full pedestrian crossing and west exit are available. Start on the visitor deck, with no road, private event or river-edge shortcut.
Notice one relationship among the deck, suspension cables and tower forms near the east end. Continue at a comfortable pace, keeping through movement clear.
At a permitted place near the middle, notice how that relationship changes with your position. Do not stop in a narrow passage, lean out or attach anything to the bridge.
Finish once at the west end and write two position records with one comparison. Continue onward to Indian Spring Park; no return crossing is included in this task or in the connecting-route total.
